messages:
Mira (Support): Hey team, I'm escalating a customer issue — they hit persistent 429s and intermittent 401s during a demo. They say they were on the free plan and suddenly started seeing "quota_exhausted" + auth failures when retrying. Root logs attached below. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Alex (Eng): Can you paste the exact error blob? free-tier quotas can cause 429s but 401s are odd unless tokens rotated or we returned a 401 after too many retries.

Mira (Support): Here's the snippet from their feedback (redacted):

```
{"time":"2027-04-12T16:02:11Z","level":"error","msg":"request failed","status":429,"body":{"error":"quota_exhausted","quota_type":"per_minute"}}
{"time":"2027-04-12T16:02:13Z","level":"warn","msg":"retry failed","status":401,"body":{"error":"invalid_api_key","detail":"token expired on retry"}}
```

Mira (Support): Repro steps they gave: 1) free-tier sign-up 2) run concurrent load from CI (20 parallel streams) 3) hit ~150 rps for 3m 4) clients automatically retried with cached token -> then started getting 401s.

Jordan (SRE): Sounds like two separate failure modes layered: free-tier per-minute cap -> 429s; client retries exhausted immediate quota and fallback used cached/rotated token causing 401s from our auth service. Could be their client library incorrectly reusing an expired token.

Sam (Platform): We throttle at per-account level: Free plan = 6,000 tokens/min and 100 requests/min (example limits per docs). If they hit 150 rps sustained we'd absolutely trigger 429s. Suggest we check their account_id for recent auth events and token rotation logs.

Alex (Eng): Quick mitigation options: 1) issue a short-lived temporary burst lift (support action) for the demo, 2) advise sales on a sales-assisted upgrade to paid tier, or 3) ask customer to reduce concurrency + exponential backoff. For 1) we need approval from Sales & Billing.

Mira (Support): Customer is mid-demo with paying prospects — they asked for an immediate temporary lift for the next 45 minutes. They also reported costs concerns so might prefer short-term lift over full upgrade.

Anne (Sales): @Mira (Support) I can approve a one-off demo burst once Billing verifies there's no unpaid invoice. Ping me the account_id and expected qps. I'll also offer a trial of the Basic Paid plan (30 day) if they want. :thumbsup:

Billing-bot: Automated check: account_id redacted-12345 has no outstanding invoices, billing status: active, plan: free. (reaction: :white_check_mark:)

Mira (Support): Account ID redacted-12345. They expect ~200 rps peak for 30 mins (token-heavy workloads).

Jordan (SRE): Operational note: temporary lift is doable but we should avoid global config changes. Recommended flow: create a scoped policy override for this account, set per-minute request cap to 12,000 for 60 minutes, enable verbose auth logging, and set fallback rule to reject retries that use expired tokens with a clear 401 message. I can prepare the override and a rollback timer.

Alex (Eng): Also propose adding a helper in support reply with repro-safe curl and client guidance: set `Retry-After` backoff, rotate token proactively, and prefer streaming when possible. Example curl to reproduce with small concurrency: 

```
for i in {1..40}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' &
done
wait
```

Mira (Support): I'll send that guidance. For the 401s, customer says their token refresh service sometimes returns the previous token until it reaches eventual consistency (internal bug on their side). I told them to check refresh TTLs.

Anne (Sales): I'll message customer with two paths: 1) temporary burst today while they complete the demo (approve 60 mins), 2) a sales-enabled upgrade to Basic Paid (monthly commit) with a one-time onboarding credit. If they accept the upgrade, we'll coordinate with Platform to migrate traffic and avoid manual overrides.

Sam (Platform): FYI: If Sales opts to upgrade mid-demo, we can automate capacity increase via the billing webhook that flips their plan. That will be safer than a manual override. We need Sales to confirm via the billing flow.

Mira (Support): Action items: 1) @Anne (Sales) confirm approval (she already said yes) 2) @Jordan (SRE) create the scoped override and set rollback timer 3) @Alex (Eng) draft customer-facing troubleshooting steps + the curl repro 4) I'll notify the customer and close loop.

Jordan (SRE): Scoped override created: policy-id: temp-burst-1793024680, effective: +60m, new caps: 12k req/min, rate-limit-mode: permissive for this account. Rollback scheduled at 2027-04-12T17:07:05Z. (Deploy-bot triggered a config change)

Deploy-bot: Config change applied to policy temp-burst-1793024680 at 2027-04-12T16:10:25Z by Jordan (SRE).

Mira (Support): Customer confirmed the demo completed successfully after we applied the lift. They did see reduced 401s after we suggested token refresh tweaks. They accepted a sales trial for Basic Paid; Anne, please follow up for contract. Closing here unless anyone needs follow-up. :tada:
